title: 189. Algebra, Equations & Inequalities: Solving Two-by-Two Linear Systems by Elimination
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Solving a two-by-two linear system by elimination
questions.learningObjective: Solve a simple linear system by adding or subtracting the equations to eliminate one variable.
questions.question: Solve the system \(x+y=5,\quad x-y=1\) by elimination.
questions.explanation: Add the two equations to eliminate \(y\): \((x+y)+(x-y)=5+1\), so \(2x=6\), giving \(x=3\). Substitute \(x=3\) into \(x+y=5\): \(3+y=5\), so \(y=2\). The solution is \((3,2)\).
questions.hint: Look for a variable whose coefficients are opposites, then add the equations.

questions.concept: Solving a two-by-two linear system by elimination
questions.learningObjective: Use elimination by addition when one pair of coefficients is opposite.
questions.question: Solve the system \(2x+y=7,\quad 3x-y=3\) by elimination.
questions.explanation: Add the equations to eliminate \(y\): \((2x+y)+(3x-y)=7+3\), so \(5x=10\), giving \(x=2\). Substitute \(x=2\) into \(2x+y=7\): \(4+y=7\), so \(y=3\). The solution is \((2,3)\).
questions.hint: The \(y\)-terms have opposite coefficients, so add the two equations first.

questions.concept: Solving a two-by-two linear system by elimination
questions.learningObjective: Multiply one equation before eliminating a variable.
questions.question: Solve the system \(2x+3y=12,\quad x-y=1\) by elimination.
questions.explanation: Multiply the second equation by \(2\): \(2x-2y=2\). Subtract this from the first equation: \((2x+3y)-(2x-2y)=12-2\), so \(5y=10\), giving \(y=2\). Substitute \(y=2\) into \(x-y=1\): \(x-2=1\), so \(x=3\). The solution is \((3,2)\).
questions.hint: Multiply the second equation so that the \(x\)-coefficients match, then subtract.

questions.concept: Solving a two-by-two linear system by elimination
questions.learningObjective: Eliminate one variable after multiplying an equation by a constant.
questions.question: Solve the system \(3x+2y=16,\quad x+y=6\) by elimination.
questions.explanation: Multiply the second equation by \(2\): \(2x+2y=12\). Subtract this from the first equation: \((3x+2y)-(2x+2y)=16-12\), so \(x=4\). Substitute \(x=4\) into \(x+y=6\): \(4+y=6\), so \(y=2\). The solution is \((4,2)\).
questions.hint: Multiply \(x+y=6\) by \(2\) to match the \(y\)-coefficients, then subtract.

questions.concept: Solving a two-by-two linear system by elimination
questions.learningObjective: Apply elimination to a simple word problem involving two numbers.
questions.question: The sum of two numbers is \(12\), and their difference is \(4\). Solve the system \(x+y=12,\quad x-y=4\) by elimination. What is the ordered pair \((x,y)\)?
questions.explanation: Add the two equations: \((x+y)+(x-y)=12+4\), so \(2x=16\), giving \(x=8\). Substitute \(x=8\) into \(x+y=12\): \(8+y=12\), so \(y=4\). The solution is \((8,4)\).
questions.hint: Since the \(y\)-terms are opposites, add the equations to eliminate \(y\).

questions.concept: Solving a two-by-two linear system by elimination
questions.learningObjective: Solve a linear system by multiplying both equations before eliminating a variable.
questions.question: Solve the system \(2x+5y=20,\quad 3x+2y=19\) by elimination.
questions.explanation: Multiply the first equation by \(3\): \(6x+15y=60\). Multiply the second equation by \(2\): \(6x+4y=38\). Subtract the second result from the first: \((6x+15y)-(6x+4y)=60-38\), so \(11y=22\), giving \(y=2\). Substitute \(y=2\) into \(2x+5y=20\): \(2x+10=20\), so \(2x=10\) and \(x=5\). The solution is \((5,2)\).
questions.hint: Multiply the equations so that the \(x\)-coefficients become equal, then subtract.

questions.concept: Solving a two-by-two linear system by elimination
questions.learningObjective: Use subtraction to eliminate a variable with matching coefficients.
questions.question: Solve the system \(3x+2y=13,\quad x+2y=7\) by elimination.
questions.explanation: Subtract the second equation from the first: \((3x+2y)-(x+2y)=13-7\), so \(2x=6\), giving \(x=3\). Substitute \(x=3\) into \(x+2y=7\): \(3+2y=7\), so \(2y=4\) and \(y=2\). The solution is \((3,2)\).
questions.hint: The \(y\)-coefficients are already the same, so subtract the equations to eliminate \(y\).

questions.concept: Solving a two-by-two linear system by elimination
questions.learningObjective: Determine the number of solutions of a linear system by elimination.
questions.question: Use elimination to solve the system \(2x+3y=6,\quad 4x+6y=12\). How many solutions does the system have?
questions.explanation: Multiply the first equation by \(2\): \(4x+6y=12\). This is exactly the second equation, so the two equations represent the same line. Therefore every point on the line is a solution, and the system has infinitely many solutions.
questions.hint: Multiply the first equation by \(2\), then compare both the left-hand side and the constant with the second equation.

questions.concept: Solving a two-by-two linear system by elimination
questions.learningObjective: Solve a linear system with a fractional coefficient by first clearing the fraction.
questions.question: Solve the system \(\frac{x}{2}+y=4,\quad x-y=2\) by elimination.
questions.explanation: Multiply the first equation by \(2\): \(x+2y=8\). Subtract the second equation \(x-y=2\) from this result: \((x+2y)-(x-y)=8-2\), so \(3y=6\), giving \(y=2\). Substitute \(y=2\) into \(x-y=2\): \(x-2=2\), so \(x=4\). The solution is \((4,2)\).
questions.hint: Multiply the first equation by \(2\) to clear the fraction, then eliminate \(x\) by subtraction.

questions.concept: Solving a two-by-two linear system by elimination
questions.learningObjective: Use elimination to find a linear combination of the variables in a system.
questions.question: For the system \(3x+2y=16,\quad 2x+3y=14\), what is the value of \(x+y\)?
questions.explanation: Add the two equations: \((3x+2y)+(2x+3y)=16+14\), so \(5x+5y=30\). Divide both sides by \(5\): \(x+y=6\).
questions.hint: Add the equations and then factor the left-hand side to relate the result to \(x+y\).
